A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SkillSight and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary appendices. Their shared content and additions support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original skill-classification results on three datasets, component and loss ablations, and quantitative gaze-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds an EgoPPG comparison, input-modality ablations, and action-level accuracy analysis.

M1.justification: The teacher architecture, student distillation procedure, and losses in Section 3 remain unchanged. Head motion was already included in v1's input definition. The newly evaluated restricted-input variants are ablations, rather than revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Ego-Exo4D, Multi-Sense Badminton, and Expert-Novice Soccer with the same skill-assessment tasks. The added comparisons and action breakdown remain within existing coverage; no new dataset, domain, or task is established.

E2.justification: Section 4, footnote 2 adds a reported comparison against EgoPPG, which v1 cited without reporting a performance comparison. Existing comparator sets remain intact. Table 2's Motion-only and Motion+Gaze rows are renamed Body-motion-only and Body-motion+Gaze, not replaced.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on EgoPPG's modified Ego-Exo4D test set, restricted-input controls, and an action-level analysis using clustered atomic-action captions. The modified test set is explicitly distinguished from Table 1's setting. Existing main-experiment splits, metrics, clip sampling, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds gaze-direction versus head-rotation ablations; Appendix C adds evaluation without translation; Appendix F and Figure 8 examine accuracy across atomic actions. These targeted additions supplement the retained component, loss, and gaze-behavior analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds. Figure 6 retains its existing error-bar presentation, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values. New results include 41.4/41.8/44.4 for gaze-only/head-motion-only/combined distilled inputs, action accuracies in Figure 8, and reported relative advantages over EgoPPG of 11% for SkillSight-T and 0.5% for SkillSight-S on the modified test set. Appendix C also reports 44.4% without translation, but its claimed 0.4% drop is not reconciled with the retained 44.4% headline result.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, attention and distillation equations, normalization definitions, and power model remain unchanged. The additions introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims about gaze-based skill assessment, the teacher–student framework, accuracy, and power efficiency. The introduction's added contrast with tabletop activities restates the dynamic-versus-static distinction already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as supporting complementary gaze and head-motion information. Appendix F extends the existing subtle-movement limitation by distinguishing perception-driven actions from fine motor execution. Appendix C discusses the SLAM-camera dependency of recorded translation and a possible IMU-only alternative.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 newly specifies three source wearable devices and 21 joint positions for the soccer body-motion input. Appendix C clarifies dataset-dependent modality inclusion and the visual-inertial odometry source of translation. These are documentation additions; existing hyperparameters, hardware details, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Peng et al., In the Eye of MLLM, to the discussion of gaze-based intention understanding. The already-cited EgoPPG receives an explicit empirical comparison. The broader research positioning remains stable; most reference-number changes follow the single added citation.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited prose and terminology refinements, expands the affiliation, adds acknowledgements, and adds explanatory appendix paragraphs and Section F. The main narrative and section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 8's action-accuracy bar chart, expands Figure 5's caption, relabels Table 2's motion rows, and reflows appendix content. Existing figures and tables are otherwise retained, with no broad visual redesign. Page-number footers are removed.

improvement.justification: The new modality controls, action-level analysis, and EgoPPG comparison provide useful supporting evidence absent from v1, while the sensor-source disclosure improves transparency. The gains are limited by sparse details for the new comparison and the unresolved relationship between Appendix C's 44.4% result, its claimed 0.4% drop, and Table 1. Overall, the additions modestly improve the paper's evidential support and clarity.
